memory_lessons.applicability: Contiguous-x stencil loops on this frozen build; alignment still needs measurement and confirmation.
memory_lessons.claim: Recorded valid guarded-SIMD candidates measured around 0.079–0.083 s, while the two scalar formulations measured around 0.453–0.468 s. The 16-byte-aligned candidate was slightly faster than the unaligned candidate, whereas the 64-byte-aligned candidate was slower; these measurements motivate testing 32-byte alignment but do not establish an alignment optimum.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this runtime-checked 32-byte peel under the official protocol; compare it with the 16-byte and unaligned candidates, and independently confirm any selected leader.

proposal.hypothesis: Among the recorded valid SIMD candidates, runtime-peeled 16-byte alignment measured 0.079254 s, guarded SIMD without an alignment clause measured 0.079892 s, and 64-byte alignment measured 0.087704 s. This candidate tests an intermediate 32-byte boundary: each contiguous interior row checks the actual residues of input, velocity, and output pointers, scalar-peels to a common aligned start when possible, and otherwise uses unaligned guarded SIMD. It makes no ISA or allocation-alignment assumption, and the close 16-byte/unaligned results are not evidence of a stable gain.

retained: Keep the timestep kernel unfused and preserve the existing x/y/z interior bounds and stencil arithmetic order.
Form each x-line pointer from row_base + x0 so the interior offset is included in the runtime alignment check.

For OpenMP 4.0+ builds, verify that input, velocity, and output row pointers share a residue modulo 32 bytes; peel scalar cells to a common 32-byte boundary and use an aligned OpenMP SIMD loop when the peel fits.
Use an unaligned OpenMP SIMD loop when residues differ or the required peel is unsuitable; use the scalar loop if the OpenMP SIMD guard is unavailable.
Do not change compiler flags, assume an ISA extension, add threading, or add spatial or temporal blocking.
